All three render cleanly. Screenshots under `prototypes/` (live: `edge.html?state=long`, `?state=toread-empty`, `?state=archived-empty`).

**Very long text and many tags** (`shot-41-edge-long-content.png`)
A bookmark with an absurdly long title, description, note, twelve tags and a long URL still reads comfortably: the title wraps, the description is trimmed to **three lines on the card** (the full text shows when you open/edit it), tags wrap onto multiple rows, and the long URL wraps instead of overflowing. Nothing pushes the card out of shape.

**"To read" when you're all caught up** (`shot-42-edge-toread-empty.png`)
Rather than a blank list, you get a reassuring *"You're all caught up — nothing left to read"* with a pointer to All / Finished.

**"Archived" when nothing's archived** (`shot-43-edge-archived-empty.png`)
A gentle note explaining what archiving is for, instead of emptiness.

Two questions:

1. Is trimming the **description to ~3 lines on the card** (full text on open/edit) the right call, or would you rather see the whole thing on every card?
2. These empty-state messages — do they strike the right tone, or would you prefer something plainer?

And one I can't easily show but should confirm in words: when your library grows to **hundreds or thousands of bookmarks**, do you want the list to **load more as you scroll** (keeping it fast), rather than rendering everything at once? I'd treat the *speed* target itself as a separate quality concern to tune later, but I want to confirm the *behaviour* of loading in chunks is acceptable.
